ZetaAqr.no_rv_data_note: Tokovinin (2016) states there are no RV data of adequate precision for this system's inner orbit; neither formalism uses any RV data here, so no dynamical component masses can be derived for ZetaAqr in either formalism -- this is a data limitation shared by both, not a formalism failure.

orbit3.canonical_benchmark_chi2_note: final_chi2 above is recomputed by this script's own zetaaqr_orbit3_fit(), not copied from run_orbit3_benchmark(); canonical_benchmark_chi2 is the live value from that canonical benchmark path (the one docs/paper_reference_notes.md Section 3.3 cites, 694.51), checked to agree within 0.5 every time this script runs -- see the 2026-08-30 fix note at this module's ZETA_EXPECTED loading block. A 2026-08-30 investigation found and fixed a real ~5-point divergence between these two numbers, traced to this script previously initializing the outer orbit from ZetaAqr.in2's raw file header (T02=1980.5) instead of from the literature/expected_results value (T02=1981.50) -- see docs/project_decisions.md's dated entry for the full investigation.

legacy.rv_discarded_note: Legacy ORBITT2 has no mechanism to use radial-velocity data at all (LEGACY_TRIPLE_PARAMETER_ORDER and triple_visual_residuals() carry no K1/K2/K3/K4/V0 handling) -- this is a structural limitation of the formalism as implemented, not a choice made for this comparison.

a_B_degeneracy_diagnostics.interpretation: The published/expected wobble amplitude for this system is negative (f * a_true = -0.33 * 0.0385 ~= -0.0127 arcsec), but legacy inner.a is bounded to [0, +inf) in triple_bounds.build_triple_bounds() and so cannot represent a negative wobble amplitude. The optimizer's best available compromise is to drive inner.a toward its lower bound of 0 (minimizing the unavoidable sign-error penalty in the 110-observation 'outer+inner' visual stream that inner.a alone controls), which in turn lets the 13-observation 'B*inner' stream be satisfied by an arbitrarily large B (since the product B*a can stay near its fitted finite value even as a -> 0 and B -> infinity in tandem). The raw fitted values (a_fitted ~= 2.7e-8, essentially at a_lower_bound=0.0; B_fitted ~= 1.73e6) already show this directly. The formal diagnostics corroborate a severe, genuine non-identifiability in this fit overall -- condition_number ~= 2.3e42 (double-precision arithmetic is only meaningful to ~1e16 dynamic range, so this matrix is numerically singular) and effective_rank collapsing to 5 of 15 fitted parameters (is_degenerate=True) -- but the specific per-parameter breakdown in worst_constrained_mode_loadings /  dominant_parameters_in_worst_mode should NOT be over-interpreted as 'a and B are the degenerate pair': at this condition number the eigenvector decomposition itself is numerically unreliable (expected, since a's Jacobian column is suppressed to ~1e-8 by a_fitted's own near-zero value, which is exactly the kind of ill-conditioning that produces spurious eigenvector mixing with unrelated parameters such as T0/P). The defensible, honestly-reported claim is therefore: (1) a is pinned at its lower bound, (2) B is consequently left essentially unconstrained and explodes, and (3) the fit as a whole is formally degenerate (condition_number, effective_rank, is_degenerate all corroborate this) -- not a specific claim about which eigenmode 'contains' the a/B pair.

B_fit_vs_reciprocal_of_f_fit.note: f_fitted is negative for this system (published f=-0.33; see docs/project_decisions.md's 'f unbounded' entry), so 1/f_fitted is negative -- but B is bounded to [0, +inf) in triple_bounds.build_triple_bounds() and so cannot reach that value directly. In practice the legacy optimizer does NOT pin B at its lower bound of 0 (check B_at_lower_bound above -- it is False): instead it drives inner.a toward 0 and lets B grow essentially without bound as a consequence, an a/B degeneracy specific to this negative-wobble system. See legacy.a_B_degeneracy_diagnostics above for the formal (condition-number/rank/degeneracy) characterization of this finding -- this comparison is therefore NOT a clean B=1/f validation for HIP111805 the way it is for ZetaAqr; it is a genuine, investigated discrepancy rooted in B's bound excluding the physically correct negative value.

comparison.chi2_not_directly_comparable_note: Legacy final_chi2 is computed over 110 visual observations only (see legacy.observations_used); ORBIT3 final_chi2 is computed over 110 visual + 93 RV observations = 203 total (see orbit3.observations_used). The two chi2 values are NOT on the same footing and must not be interpreted as 'legacy fits better' or worse without accounting for this.
